# Evidence Loom for After-Hours Dental Lab Master Spec Prompt

Build Evidence Loom for After-Hours Dental Lab as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for after-hours dental lab.
Use Evidence Loom as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic health templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: weaves scattered proof into a single inspectable decision trail for after-hours dental lab, using case trays, shade photos, and remake approvals.
- Primary workflow: intake night-shift ceramic crown remakes into a photo proof set while respecting offline-capable constraints
- Signature interaction: drag evidence chips into a timeline and watch missing links glow

## Required Shape
- First screen: Photo Proof Set workbench
- Hero controls: Intake, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: case trays, shade photos, and remake approvals

## Service Boundary
- Keep photo proof set state in a service; UI submits intake commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Evidence Loom for After-Hours Dental Lab' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: offline-capable workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for after-hours dental lab and keep Evidence Loom as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Photo Proof Set workbench and keep the visible controls to Intake, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Photo Proof Set workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep photo proof set state in a service; UI submits intake commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for case trays, shade photos, and remake approvals so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of offline-capable workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Evidence Loom for After-Hours Dental Lab' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Evidence Loom for After-Hours Dental Lab to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for intake and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.

submissionEnvelope.seedPrompt:
# Trust Ledger for After-Hours Dental Lab Master Spec Prompt

Build Trust Ledger for After-Hours Dental Lab as a first-shot NexusCentral concept for after-hours dental lab.
Use Trust Ledger as the original lens and keep the project distinct from generic health templates.

## Product Brief
- Why this exists: shows who approved what and why before work moves forward for after-hours dental lab, using case trays, shade photos, and remake approvals.
- Primary workflow: plan night-shift ceramic crown remakes into a route manifest while respecting role-scoped constraints
- Signature interaction: approval cards with source snapshots

## Required Shape
- First screen: Route Manifest workbench
- Hero controls: Plan, Review, Save state
- Advanced controls: Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals
- Starter data: case trays, shade photos, and remake approvals

## Service Boundary
- Keep route manifest state in a service; UI submits plan commands and subscribes to progress.
- Keep the UI thin and let services own state, queues, and progress.
- Do not make the visible shell responsible for real work.

## NexusCentral Surfaces
- Validate across: Lab, Workspaces
- Harness question: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Trust Ledger for After-Hours Dental Lab' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- Risk note: role-scoped workflow may need fixtures before real validation.

## 11-Part Sprint
- 1. Frame the world: Write the product brief for after-hours dental lab and keep Trust Ledger as the unique lens.
- 2. Lock the first screen: Center the UI on Route Manifest workbench and keep the visible controls to Plan, Review, Save state.
- 3. Define the state model: Write the service-owned records, statuses, and audit events for the Route Manifest workflow.
- 4. Separate commands from display: Map UI commands into service calls using the rule: Keep route manifest state in a service; UI submits plan commands and subscribes to progress.
- 5. Add intake and fixture modes: Make import and sample-data flows for case trays, shade photos, and remake approvals so the app can be exercised without live inputs.
- 6. Tune the hero and advanced controls: Keep the hero controls simple and move Import fixture data, Export evidence, Configure approvals into foldouts or settings.
- 7. Handle errors and recovery: Write exception, retry, and recovery behavior for the risk of role-scoped workflow may need fixtures before real validation..
- 8. Map validation surfaces: Cover Lab, Workspaces with a small probe plan and keep the harness question explicit: Ask the Codex CLI read-only harness to review whether 'Trust Ledger for After-Hours Dental Lab' can be built as a thin UI over service-owned state.
- 9. Draft the seed prompt: Write a master spec prompt that could hand Trust Ledger for After-Hours Dental Lab to a builder in one shot.
- 10. Write acceptance criteria: Turn the build into a testable first-release checklist for plan and the surrounding workflow.
- 11. Bundle the intake packet: Assemble all fields into a single profile packet so the next pass can submit the full idea at once.

## Definition of Done
- The first screen is focused and buildable.
- The profile has a service-owned state model.
- The app can be batch-submitted from one packed record.
- The idea is unique enough that a builder would not confuse it with another catalog item.

## Builder Rule
Build the full profile in one pass using the sprint above as the implementation order.
